stage: Stage 2/3 — BOM generation, review and approval
intro: API test cases in the order the process actually runs — intake breakdown → style attachment & pattern → BOM generation → the BOM review/approval lifecycle → notifications → admin setup → full regression. Ready-made requests: bom.postman_collection.json.
notes: No list/search-BOMs endpoint exists — every BOM case needs a `bom_id` you already have (from seed data or a prior response).
There is no "Pattern Maker" role in the codebase. For wrong-role cases use any seeded role outside cutting_manager / direct_manager / managing_director — e.g. Lining Manager or Office Viewer.
`direct_manager` currently bypasses every MD-only gate (approve/reject/export/reopen, and every `/admin/*` route) via the superuser policy.

**Error shapes are inconsistent**: role checks, 401s and most router-level pre-checks return `{"detail": "..."}`; most lifecycle errors raised in the service layer return `{"error": "...", "message"?: "..."}`. Check both.
A non-UUID path parameter returns a generic 422 from FastAPI's path parsing, before any handler runs — distinct from a 404 for a well-formed but nonexistent id.
`base_revision` is `ge=1`; always substitute the BOM's real current revision from a fresh GET (the old checked-in example shipped 0, which always fails).

**D-L2 / E-L1:** approve only checks that `cutting_confirmed_at` is set — it never re-checks status, and reject never clears it. Approving a rejected-but-previously-confirmed BOM is expected to return 200 today; confirm and flag.
**Q-B1:** a check rule with a single-element `range` array passes schema validation then crashes the handler with an unhandled IndexError → HTTP 500. Confirmed defect.
**R-L1:** an unrecognized `garment_type_code` is not rejected — it silently falls back to "applies to any garment type".
The admin cost-catalog and checks GETs read a process-local cache that is not refreshed on a TTL despite the comments — under multiple workers, PUT-then-GET can appear not to have taken effect.

cases.title: Edit Unit Price on a Draft BOM
cases.expected: {"revision": base_revision+1, "recomputed": {...}, "reconfirm_required": false} (cf. EI-P1)

cases.title: Edit DCM on a leather line

cases.title: Edit several cells, save once
steps: PATCH .../items — edits array with 3 entries (different bom_item_id/field/value) in one call
cases.expected: 200, single call; recomputed reflects all 3 changes together.

cases.title: Edit a BOM that's Ready for Review but not yet confirmed
steps: PATCH .../items on a BOM with status = ready_for_review
cases.expected: 200 — _EDITABLE_STATES includes both draft and ready_for_review.

cases.title: Edit the DCM cell specifically (not the Qty alias)
cases.expected: 200, identical effect — the service writes both fields to the same qty_per_garment column.

cases.title: Leave Unit Price blank
cases.expected: 422 Pydantic validation error — "value" is a required field on each edit.

cases.title: Negative quantity
cases.expected: {"error":"negative_value","bom_item_id":...,"field":"qty_per_garment","value":-5} (cf. EI-N7)

cases.title: Non-numeric text in a numeric cell
cases.expected: 422 — fails FastAPI's float coercion before it reaches the service layer (generic Pydantic error shape, not the custom invalid_value error).

cases.title: Two testers edit the same BOM at once
steps: Both GET the BOM, note revision N
Session B: PATCH .../items {"base_revision":N,...} on a different line → sent after A
cases.expected: Session A: 200. Session B: {"error":"stale_revision","current_revision":N+1} — enforced twice (pre-check and an atomic claim_revision at commit). (cf. EI-N8/N12)

cases.title: Try to edit an Approved/Locked/Exported BOM
steps: PATCH .../items on a BOM with status in {approved, locked, exported}
cases.expected: {"error":"bom_locked","message":"A locked/approved BOM rejects all edits."}

cases.title: Try to edit a Rejected BOM
steps: PATCH .../items on a BOM with status = rejected
cases.expected: {"error":"bom_rejected","message":"Reopen the rejected BOM before editing."}

cases.title: Wrong role reaches the edit screen
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted, same shape as A-N2.

cases.title: Qty set to exactly 0
cases.expected: 200 — 0 is the legal floor, only negative values are rejected.

cases.title: Unreasonably large price
cases.expected: 200, accepted with no ceiling — flag as a possible missing sanity check server-side too.

cases.title: Smallest possible edit
steps: PATCH .../items — edits array with exactly one entry
cases.expected: 200 — a single-item batch is a valid request.

cases.title: Change the same cell twice before saving
steps: Not separately API-testable — the client only ever sends the final chosen value in one PATCH call; there is no server-side "history" of unsent edits to probe.
cases.expected: Confirm only that a single PATCH with value:15 stores 15 — nothing else to assert at the API layer.

cases.title: High-precision price
cases.expected: PATCH → 200. Follow-up GET → unit_price still shows full precision, not rounded.

cases.title: Non-material lines don't get the "Manual" stamp
steps: PATCH .../items — edit a Thread or Accessory category line's qty_per_garment
cases.expected: 200; that line's dcm_source is untouched — the manual stamp only applies to main/sub-material, lining and interlining categories.

cases.title: Editing DCM after Confirm Cutting re-opens the gate
steps: PATCH .../items — edit "dcm" or "qty_per_garment" on a material line
cases.expected: 200; response has "reconfirm_required": true, recomputed.status:"draft", cutting_confirmed_at cleared. (cf. EI-L2)

cases.title: A price-only edit does NOT re-open the gate
steps: On the same confirmed BOM, PATCH .../items — edit only "unit_price"
cases.expected: 200; "reconfirm_required": false, status stays ready_for_review.

cases.title: Totals stay in sync with edits
cases.expected: 200; recomputed.garment_fob_price and recomputed.bulk_total both reflect the change in the same response.

cases.title: Revision counter never skips
steps: PATCH .../items three times in a row, each time using the "revision" returned by the previous call as the next base_revision
cases.expected: Each response's "revision" is exactly +1 over the last — no skips, no repeats.

cases.title: Confirm a Draft BOM
cases.expected: {"bom_id":..., "status":"ready_for_review", "cutting_confirmed_at":..., "templates_backfilled":N, "notifications_created":N} (cf. CC-P1)

cases.title: Re-click Confirm Cutting on an already-confirmed BOM
cases.expected: 200 again — draft and ready_for_review are both allowed states; cutting_confirmed_at is refreshed.

cases.title: Try on an Approved/Locked/Exported BOM
steps: POST .../confirm-cutting on status in {approved, locked, exported}
cases.expected: {"error":"invalid_state_for_confirmation","current_status":...,"message":"Cutting confirmation is only allowed on a draft BOM."}

cases.title: Try on a Rejected BOM
cases.expected: Same invalid_state_for_confirmation error, current_status:"rejected".

cases.title: Wrong role
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted.

cases.title: BOM with only non-material lines
steps: POST .../confirm-cutting on a BOM with only thread/accessory/packaging lines
cases.expected: 200, "templates_backfilled": 0 — nothing to remember, but no error.

cases.title: Confirm while a material line's DCM is still 0
steps: Leave a material line's qty_per_garment at 0
cases.expected: 200 — the endpoint doesn't block on a provisional 0; worth flagging as a possible product-level gap.

cases.title: Confirmed values become the "remembered" template
steps: POST .../confirm-cutting, note the confirmed qty_per_garment for a style/size
Generate a new BOM for the same style/size (endpoint not confirmed by source read — likely under a /specs or /styles route; locate it before testing)
cases.expected: New BOM's matching material line pre-fills from the confirmed value instead of starting blank.

cases.title: Reviewer notification carries the right context
steps: Fetch the MD's notification (endpoint not covered by this report — check /api/v1 for a notifications route)
cases.expected: Notification text names the correct style and order number, not a generic message.

cases.title: Approve a confirmed BOM
cases.expected: {"bom_id":..., "status":"approved", "inventory_check_id":...} (cf. AP-P1)

cases.title: Approve and Lock
cases.expected: {"status":"locked", ...} instead of "approved".

cases.title: Direct Manager approves
cases.expected: 200 — DM is in the superuser bypass set, so this succeeds even though the endpoint is nominally MD-only. (cf. AP-L5)

cases.title: Try to Approve before cutting is confirmed
steps: POST .../approve on a BOM where cutting_confirmed_at is null
cases.expected: {"error":"cutting_confirmation_required","message":"The cutting manager must confirm the BOM before approval."}

cases.title: Cutting Manager tries to reach the review panel
cases.expected: 403 — cutting_manager isn't in the MD-or-DM gate and has no bypass here.

cases.title: Double-click / re-approve an already-Approved BOM
steps: POST .../approve again on a BOM already status = approved
cases.expected: 200 again — approve_bom only checks cutting_confirmed_at, not current status, so a repeat call succeeds without error.

cases.title: Approve still completes if the inventory check fails behind the scenes
steps: POST .../approve on a BOM likely to trip an inventory-check edge case
cases.expected: 200 "approved" regardless — the inventory check runs best-effort and its failure is swallowed/logged, not surfaced as a request error; inventory_check_id may come back null.

cases.title: [Verify] Approve shouldn't be reachable on a Rejected BOM
steps: Get a BOM to status = rejected that was cutting-confirmed beforehand (cutting_confirmed_at is not cleared by reject)
cases.expected: Per source: approve_bom() never re-checks bom.status — only cutting_confirmed_at. Expect 200 "approved" even though status is "rejected". This is a real backend gap, not UI-only — confirm and report as a finding regardless of what any UI does to hide the button.

cases.title: Reject with a reason
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id}/reject — {"reason":"Leather grade mismatch vs. spec"} (status = ready_for_review)
cases.expected: {"bom_id":..., "status":"rejected", "rejection_reason":"Leather grade mismatch vs. spec"} (cf. RJ-P1)

cases.title: Direct Manager rejects
cases.expected: 200 — DM bypass, same as MD.

cases.title: Try to confirm with no reason
steps: POST .../reject — {"reason":""} or the "reason" key omitted entirely
cases.expected: 422 — Pydantic's min_length=1 rejects an empty string / missing field.

cases.title: Reason is only spaces
cases.expected: Passes Pydantic (3 chars, non-empty) but caught server-side: {"error":"reason_required","message":"A rejection reason is required."}

cases.title: Try to Reject a Draft BOM
cases.expected: {"error":"not_ready_for_review","current_status":"draft"} — reject is only valid from ready_for_review.

cases.title: Try to Reject an Approved/Locked/Exported BOM
steps: POST .../reject on status in {approved, locked, exported}
cases.expected: {"error":"bom_locked","message":"An approved BOM cannot be rejected."}

cases.title: Try to Reject a BOM that's already Rejected
cases.expected: {"error":"not_ready_for_review","current_status":"rejected"}

cases.title: Cutting Manager tries to Reject
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted.

cases.title: 1-character reason
cases.expected: 200, accepted.

cases.title: Reason with extra spaces
cases.expected: POST → 200. GET's rejection_reason should read "wrong color" trimmed — the source read confirmed reject_bom checks reason.strip() for emptiness but did not confirm whether the stored value itself is trimmed or raw; verify this directly against the GET response.

cases.title: Very long reason
cases.expected: Both calls 200; GET's rejection_reason returns the full text, not truncated.

cases.title: Cutting-confirmed state silently survives a rejection
steps: POST .../reject on a BOM that had already passed confirm-cutting
cases.expected: POST → 200 rejected. GET afterward: cutting_confirmed_at is still populated — reject_bom does not clear it. This is the same underlying fact that makes D-L2 possible; confirm both together.

cases.title: Reopen a Rejected BOM
cases.expected: {"bom_id":..., "status":"draft", "revision": <previous+1>} (cf. RO-P1)

cases.title: Try to Reopen a BOM that isn't Rejected
steps: POST .../reopen on status in {draft, ready_for_review, approved, locked, exported}
cases.expected: {"error":"not_rejected","current_status":...}

cases.title: Cutting Manager tries to Reopen
cases.expected: 403 — cutting_manager has no bypass on this gate (only direct_manager/managing_director are allowed).

cases.title: Double-click Reopen
cases.expected: First call: 200 → draft. Second call: 409 {"error":"not_rejected","current_status":"draft"} — sequential calls fail safely rather than double-incrementing; true simultaneous requests may race, worth trying both ways.

cases.title: Approve is correctly re-blocked after Reopen
steps: POST .../approve on the same bom_id, without re-running confirm-cutting
cases.expected: Reopen clears cutting_confirmed_at, so approve returns {"error":"cutting_confirmation_required",...} — the D-L2 loophole is closed once reopen actually runs.

cases.title: Grid is fully editable immediately after Reopen
cases.expected: 200 — draft is an editable state, no residual lock from the prior rejected status.

cases.title: Export an Approved BOM
cases.expected: {"bom_id":..., "status":"exported", "export_document_id":..., "sha256":..., "mime":..., "storage_url":...} (cf. EX-P1)

cases.title: Export a Locked BOM
cases.expected: Same result — status → "exported".

cases.title: Re-export an already-Exported BOM
cases.expected: 200 with the same export_document_id and sha256 — idempotent short-circuit, no regeneration.

cases.title: Direct Manager exports
cases.expected: 200 — DM bypass, same as MD.

cases.title: Try to Export a Draft/Ready-for-Review/Rejected BOM
steps: POST .../export on status in {draft, ready_for_review, rejected}
cases.expected: {"error":"not_approved","message":"Export is only allowed from an approved/locked BOM."}

cases.title: Cutting Manager tries to Export
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted.

cases.title: Two BOMs that export to an identical document
cases.expected: Both 200; the "sha256" values match and the export dedupes to the same stored file.

cases.title: Exported PDF carries the right approval details
steps: GET the "storage_url" from the response and download the PDF
cases.expected: The PDF itself (not the JSON) shows the approver's name, approval date, style name and order number — this needs a binary fetch + manual/PDF-text check, not just a JSON assertion.

cases.title: "Exported at" doesn't move on a repeat export
steps: POST .../export, then GET /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id} and note exported_at
POST .../export again later, GET the BOM again
cases.expected: exported_at is identical across both GETs — the idempotent re-export path doesn't touch the timestamp.

sections.title: Full-flow regression scenarios
sections.sub: Chained calls across the endpoints above.

cases.title: Happy path, start to finish
cases.expected: Status walks draft → ready_for_review → approved → exported with a 200 (or the expected success shape) at every step and no 4xx along the golden path.

cases.title: Reject → Reopen → resubmit
steps: Login MD → POST /boms/{bom_id}/reject {"reason":"..."} (status must be ready_for_review)
cases.expected: Every call 200 in sequence; the BOM is fully re-usable after one rejection cycle — no 409 anywhere in this chain if done in order.

cases.title: Two testers, same BOM, same moment
steps: Both sessions GET /boms/{bom_id}, note the same revision N
Fire both PATCH /boms/{bom_id}/items calls (different bom_item_id/field) with base_revision:N within a few seconds of each other
cases.expected: Exactly one PATCH returns 200; the other returns 409 stale_revision. Neither edit is silently dropped or silently merged.

cases.title: Claim a COMPLETE submission for breakdown
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/submissions/{submission_id}/order-breakdown (submission status = COMPLETE, no OrderStyle rows yet)
cases.expected: {"submission_id":..., "status":"queued", "task_id":...} — claims the submission (status → CONSUMED) and enqueues bom.build_order_breakdown_for_submission.

cases.title: Read the breakdown once it's ready
steps: GET /api/v1/procurement/submissions/{submission_id}/order-breakdown (after the Celery task has completed)
cases.expected: {"status":"ready", "styles":[{style_signature, style_name, qty, per_size_qty, colors[], spec_match_status, dxf_match_status, ...}]}

cases.title: Poll while the breakdown is still processing
steps: Immediately after I-P1's POST, GET the same submission's order-breakdown before the worker finishes
cases.expected: {"status":"processing", "styles":[]} — submission status is already CONSUMED but no OrderStyle rows exist yet.

cases.title: Claim a submission that isn't COMPLETE
steps: POST .../order-breakdown on a submission still OPEN/QUEUED/REJECTED (order or spec doc not yet accepted)
cases.expected: Plain-string detail (not the {"error","message"} dict shape): {"detail":"submission not ready: order document not accepted, or already claimed"}

cases.title: Claim a nonexistent submission_id
cases.expected: Same 409 as I-N1, not a 404 — breakdown_state() treats a missing row the same as "not_started", so a bogus id and a genuinely-not-ready submission are indistinguishable from this response alone. Confirm and note as a gap.

cases.title: Read the breakdown for a nonexistent submission_id
cases.expected: 200 {"status":"not_started","styles":[]} — no 404 for a bad id on the GET side either.

cases.title: Re-POST while a claim is already processing
steps: POST .../order-breakdown a second time on a submission already claimed (status CONSUMED, no styles yet)
cases.expected: {"status":"already_processing"} — still 202, no second Celery task enqueued.

cases.title: Re-POST once styles already exist
steps: POST .../order-breakdown once OrderStyle rows already exist for this submission
cases.expected: {"status":"already_ready"} — still HTTP 202 even though nothing new happens, which reads oddly for an "already done" reply; worth a UX note if you're also reviewing the contract.

cases.title: Idempotent replay doesn't re-extract
steps: If the breakdown task is somehow re-triggered on a submission that already has OrderStyle rows, it short-circuits
cases.expected: Existing rows are replayed with warnings:["replayed"] instead of a fresh Gemini extraction — hard to trigger via HTTP alone; treat as a code-read confirmation rather than a black-box test.

cases.title: Spec/DXF auto-suggestion by name match
steps: GET .../order-breakdown for a submission whose style name unambiguously matches one existing accepted spec document for that client
cases.expected: That style's spec_match_status = "suggested" with spec_document_id populated. A style with 2+ ambiguous name matches instead has spec_match_status = "none" (falls back to manual).

cases.title: Confirm an explicit spec document
cases.expected: 200 OrderStyleOut with spec_document_id set and spec_match_status = "confirmed".

cases.title: Confirm an explicit DXF pattern
cases.expected: 200; dxf_match_status = "confirmed".

cases.title: Promote an existing suggestion with no explicit id
steps: POST .../attachments — Body: {} on a style whose spec_match_status is already "suggested"
cases.expected: 200; the previously-suggested spec_document_id is promoted to spec_match_status = "confirmed" without you having to resend the id.

cases.title: Nonexistent order_style_id
cases.expected: {"error":"order_style_not_found","order_style_id":...} — dict shape, distinct from the plain-string 404 used by generate-bom (K-N1).

cases.title: clear_spec and spec_document_id together
cases.expected: 422 Pydantic validation error — "clear_spec and spec_document_id are mutually exclusive".

cases.title: clear_dxf and pattern_reference_id together
cases.expected: 422, same mutual-exclusion validator for the DXF pair.

cases.title: Explicit id that doesn't actually exist
steps: POST .../attachments — Body: {"spec_document_id": "<a syntactically valid but nonexistent uuid>"}
cases.expected: 200, accepted with no validation — despite the endpoint's own docstring claiming ids are "validated to exist (and to belong to the same client)", the service assigns it blindly. The failure only surfaces later, inside generate-bom, as spec_bytes_missing (see K-B1). Confirm and file as a finding against the docstring.

cases.title: clear_spec detaches the link
cases.expected: 200; spec_document_id → null, spec_match_status → "none".

cases.title: No client ownership check on attachment ids
steps: Confirm a spec_document_id or pattern_reference_id that belongs to a different client than the order style
cases.expected: Accepted with no error — there is no cross-client ownership check on this endpoint at all. Combine with J-B1 as one finding: neither existence nor ownership is validated here.

cases.title: Generate a BOM for a style with no bom_id yet
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/order-styles/{order_style_id}/generate-bom (bom_id currently null; spec_match_status is "confirmed" or "none", never "suggested")
cases.expected: 202 StyleBomAccepted — the exact literal "status" value on this fresh-queue branch isn't nailed down by source alone; capture it from a real response and note it here.

cases.title: Generated BOM is reachable afterward
cases.role: Any authenticated role then Cutting Manager
steps: Wait for the Celery task to finish (order_style.bom_id becomes non-null)
cases.expected: 200 — the newly generated BOM view, status "draft".

cases.title: Re-POST once a BOM already exists for the style
steps: POST .../generate-bom again on a style whose bom_id is already set
cases.expected: {"status":"already_generated","bom_id":...} — still 202, no duplicate BOM created.

cases.title: Nonexistent order_style_id
cases.expected: {"detail":"order style not found"} — plain-string shape, unlike J-N1's dict shape for the same logical "not found" case on a sibling endpoint. Worth flagging as an inconsistency.

cases.title: Unconfirmed spec suggestion blocks generation
steps: POST .../generate-bom on a style whose spec_match_status is still "suggested" (never confirmed via J-P1/J-P3)
cases.expected: {"detail":"spec suggestion is unconfirmed — confirm or clear it before generating"} — plain string, router-level pre-check.

cases.title: Confirmed spec has no stored bytes
steps: Confirm a spec_document_id that exists but has no retrievable bytes (or the garbage id from J-B1)
cases.expected: The router's synchronous pre-checks pass, so you still get 202 — the spec_bytes_missing {"error":"spec_bytes_missing","message":"..."} error only happens inside the async Celery task and is NOT visible in this HTTP response. You cannot assert this failure from a single request; you need to poll the order style / BOM afterward or watch the realtime channel.

cases.title: DXF pattern pre-fills the generated BOM
steps: Upload a current DXF pattern for the style's signature via POST /patterns (section M) first
cases.expected: The generated BOM's material lines carry DXF-derived quantities/consumption from the current PatternExtraction row. Without a prior pattern upload, the BOM falls back to bare line-seeds with no DXF-derived qty. Cross-check against C-L1 in the BOM section — this is the mechanism behind it.

cases.title: Router vs. service error-shape inconsistency
steps: Compare K-N1/K-N2 (plain "detail" string, from router.py pre-checks) against the equivalent errors raised inside generate_bom_for_style() in the service layer (dict {"error",...} shape)
cases.expected: Confirmed inconsistency in the same logical error family across the sync/async paths of the same endpoint — file as an API-contract finding, not a test failure.

cases.title: List notifications
cases.expected: {"notifications":[{id,type,channel,subject,body,entity_type,entity_id,status,scheduled_for,sent_at,opened_at}], "unread": N} — scoped to the caller, in-app channel only, newest-unread-first, hard limit 100.

cases.title: Filter to unread only
cases.expected: 200; every returned item has opened_at: null.

cases.title: Open a notification you own
cases.expected: 200; opened_at populated, status → "opened".

cases.title: Consume the live SSE stream
Open a nonexistent notification
cases.expected: {"detail":"Notification not found."}

cases.title: Open someone else's notification
steps: As user B, POST /api/v1/procurement/notifications/{a notification whose recipient is user A}/open
cases.expected: {"detail":"Not your notification."} — this is the one endpoint in the whole module with an actual per-row ownership check.

cases.title: Open the same notification twice
steps: POST .../open again on the same id
cases.expected: First call: 200, opened_at stamped. Second call: 200, unchanged — no error, no re-stamp; genuinely idempotent.

cases.title: Second SSE connection doesn't replay already-sent items
steps: Open one SSE stream, let it drain the unread backlog (flips them PENDING→SENT)
Open a second SSE stream for the same user without opening those notifications first
cases.expected: The second connection only emits genuinely new notifications, not the already-SENT-but-unopened backlog. Meanwhile GET /notifications?unread_only=true still lists them, since it filters on opened_at not status — the two views can transiently disagree. Document this rather than treating it as a bug in your test.

cases.title: SSE needs a streaming-capable client
steps: Try GET .../notifications/stream with a plain Postman "Send" or a curl call without -N
cases.expected: The request hangs / appears to buffer indefinitely rather than returning — this is a test-tooling requirement (use curl -N or Postman's streaming/SSE support), not an API defect.

cases.title: 2-hour escalation is currently broken end-to-end
steps: Do not build a test expecting an unopened notification to trigger an escalation email after 2 hours
cases.expected: NotificationService.escalate_overdue() referenced by the Celery Beat task doesn't exist (AttributeError), and run_escalations() itself references undefined names (NameError) due to commented-out setup lines. The feature described in the module's own docstring does not currently work — confirm the Beat task fails rather than expecting it to succeed.

cases.title: Upload a DXF pattern
cases.expected: {"job_id": "<celery task id>", "channel": "pattern:SP12345"} — 202, async DXF parse enqueued.

cases.title: Uploaded pattern feeds BOM generation
steps: Wait for the parse task to finish
POST /order-styles/{a style with the same style_signature}/generate-bom (section K)
cases.expected: The generated BOM's material lines reflect this pattern's fabric matrix / DXF yields — cross-check with K-L1.

cases.title: style_signature sent as a form field instead of a query param
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/patterns — multipart body: file=<.dxf> AND a form field named style_signature (no query string)
cases.expected: Still 202, but style_signature is bound as a query parameter in the route signature (no Form(...) marker) — a form-field value is not picked up, so it resolves to None and "channel" comes back as the literal string "pattern:None". Confirm this exact behavior before relying on it.

cases.title: Non-DXF file accepted at the HTTP layer
cases.expected: 202, accepted with no content-type/extension check — it always names the stored object <uuid>.dxf regardless of actual content. Failure only happens later inside the async DXF parser, invisibly to this HTTP response.

cases.title: No file-size cap on this endpoint
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/patterns with a very large file (tens of MB+)
cases.expected: Accepted regardless of size at the HTTP/application layer — unlike the 25MB cap other upload endpoints in procurement/router.py enforce. Whatever limit you hit in practice is likely coming from infrastructure (reverse proxy / body-size limit), not this handler.

cases.title: Duplicate re-upload for the same style_signature
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/patterns?style_signature=SP1 with identical file bytes twice in a row
cases.expected: The repository code's own docstring claims a (style_signature, sha256) unique constraint turns a duplicate into a clean 409/no-op "caught upstream" — but no such catch exists anywhere in the module. Expect either an unhandled DB error surfacing as a generic Celery retry/failure, or a silent duplicate row, not the documented clean no-op. File the actual observed behavior as a finding.

cases.title: New upload supersedes the prior current pattern
steps: Upload a DXF for style_signature SP1, wait for it to become current
Upload a second, different DXF for the same SP1 + same client
cases.expected: The second pattern becomes is_current=True and the first is superseded (is_current=False); the generated BOM should reflect the newer pattern's data, not the first upload's.

cases.title: Set a species' yield factor
cases.expected: {"species":"COWHIDE","factor":1.35}

cases.title: Zero factor
cases.expected: 422 — schema requires factor gt=0.

cases.title: Negative factor
cases.expected: 422, same constraint.

cases.title: Wrong role
cases.expected: 403 — cutting_manager isn't in the DM/MD gate for any /admin/* route.

cases.title: Unusual species string
cases.expected: 200, accepted — species is a raw path string with no enum/regex constraint; any value silently creates a new row. Worth flagging as a possible data-quality gap.

cases.title: Repeat PUT upserts, doesn't duplicate
steps: PUT .../admin/dxf-yields/COWHIDE twice with different factor values
cases.expected: Second call updates the existing row in place. There's no GET for this resource to confirm directly — verify indirectly via a BOM generation that uses this species' yield, or a direct DB check.

cases.title: Upsert a fabric role
cases.expected: 200, echoes the input with status:"confirmed".

cases.title: Arbitrary role/category strings
cases.expected: 200, accepted — no server-side vocabulary check on "role"/"category". Flag as a data-integrity gap if that's unintended.

cases.title: Repeat POST with the same label upserts
steps: POST .../admin/fabric-roles twice with the same "label" but different "role"/"category"
cases.expected: Second call updates the existing row keyed on "label" rather than creating a duplicate.

cases.title: Read the cost catalog
cases.expected: 200 {"<GARMENT_CODE>":[{category,name,uom,unit_price,qty_per_garment}], "_default":[...]} — served from a process-local cache, not a live DB read.

cases.title: Replace a garment code's cost lines
cases.expected: {"garment_code":"SH100","lines":1}

cases.title: Negative unit price
cases.expected: 422 — schema requires unit_price ge=0.

cases.title: Zero qty_per_garment
cases.expected: 422 — schema requires qty_per_garment gt=0 (default is 1, but an explicit 0 still fails).

cases.title: Wrong role on GET or PUT
cases.expected: 403 on both.

cases.title: Empty lines array doesn't restore defaults
cases.expected: PUT → 200. Follow-up GET shows SH100's entry as an empty array, not a fallback to "_default" — clearing is not the same as resetting, confirm this explicitly.

cases.title: garment_code casing is normalized on write, not on read
cases.expected: The server uppercases the code before storing (key becomes "SH100") — look for it under the uppercase key, not the lowercase one you sent.

cases.title: Multi-worker cache staleness
steps: If your test environment runs multiple API worker processes, PUT on one request then immediately GET on another
cases.expected: The documented TTL-based cache refresh is not actually implemented — a PUT served by one worker may not be visible via GET on another until that worker restarts. If GET-after-PUT flakes intermittently, this is why, not a bug in your test sequencing.

cases.title: Read check rules
cases.expected: 200 [{"client_code":..., "checks":[...]}] — cached read.

cases.title: Replace a client's check rules
cases.expected: 200, rules replaced for that client_code.

cases.title: Single-element range array crashes the handler
cases.expected: Schema validation passes (list[float] has no length constraint) but the handler unconditionally indexes range[0] and range[1] — a one-element array raises an unhandled IndexError. Expect a raw 500, not a clean 4xx. This is a confirmed defect — reproduce it and file a bug, don't just log it as informational.

cases.title: range omitted entirely
steps: PUT .../admin/checks/CL01 — a rule with no "range" key at all
cases.expected: 200, accepted — both range bounds stored as null, no crash (the IndexError in Q-B1 only fires when "range" is truthy but short, not when it's absent).

cases.title: client_code casing is NOT normalized (asymmetric with cost-catalog)
cases.expected: These create/update two distinct rows rather than colliding — unlike cost-catalog's garment_code (P-B2), this endpoint does not uppercase client_code. Confirm and flag the inconsistency between the two admin endpoints.

cases.title: Read the POM dictionary
cases.expected: 200 [{"source_term":...,"pom_code":...,"language":...,"garment_type_id":...,"weight":...}], ordered by source_term — a live DB read, unlike cost-catalog/checks which are cached.

cases.title: Add a term mapping
cases.expected: 200; note the request field is "garment_type_code" but the response field is "garment_type_id" — different names for related data, don't assume symmetry when asserting the response.

cases.title: Zero or negative weight
cases.expected: 200, accepted — no ge/le bound on "weight" in the schema. Flag as a possible missing sanity check, same spirit as B-B2 in the BOM section.

cases.title: Unrecognized garment_type_code fails silently
cases.expected: 200, accepted — a garment_type_code that doesn't resolve via a lookup does NOT error; it silently falls back to garment_type_id: null ("applies to any garment type"). An operator typo here is indistinguishable from a deliberate "any garment type" mapping. Confirmed gap — worth filing, since it silently broadens scope rather than failing loudly.

cases.title: Repeat POST for the same key upserts
steps: POST .../admin/pom-dictionary twice with the same (language, source_term, garment_type_code) but a different "weight"
cases.expected: Second call updates the existing mapping in place (keyed on language + source_term + garment_type_id) rather than creating a duplicate.
